video_title: Jonathan Kuminga STARTING in Minn!?! + Warriors $150M Offer NEVER HAPPENED!

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's decision to join the Minnesota Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: I know what you are, I know what you're capable of, come here, you do it.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: What made the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday the right move for Jonathan Kuminga at this point of his career?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: There was a lot of conversation like, 'Hey man, I know what you are, I know what you're capable of, come here, you do it.' No one's in your way. In fact, we want you to go debunk all this stuff out there that people think. We want you to show the world what's the truth because I know it, because I played against you. Also, he's been in some of the situations played for the same coach in some other situations. He just has a way of identifying with Jonathan Kuminga that few could. And there's a respect factor for those two. And then past that, which I think really excited Jonathan Kuminga, was the vision defensively. Everybody's pitching offense, space, yeah that's great, but the fact that everybody there wants to play defense is a defensive group and how versatile they can be and then you have Rudy Gobert, the ability to switch a ton, and that was just really intriguing to Jonathan Kuminga of like, 'Man, I love what we can do defensively.'

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's role as a starter in Minnesota
quotes.excerpt: This was a clear-cut, you're coming in here to start at the four.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Going into camp, going into preseason, how are they viewing Jonathan Kuminga? Is he a starter, is he more of an energy guy?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: This was a clear-cut, you're coming in here to start at the four with Anthony Edwards, Chris Finch, Jaden McDaniels, Jonathan Kuminga, Rudy Gobert. Obviously, they have great young guys coming into, you got Ime Udoka, you got Terrence Shannon Jr., Dante when he comes back. So they pitched a great clear role. And for Jonathan Kuminga going into year six, which it's crazy it's year six now, but he's never got to come into the season going, 'I know I'm the starter.' That tailwind of just clear, 'Hey man, you're coming in here to start,' Chris Finch did a great job explaining the role to him that he envisions and how they want to play.

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Clarifying the false reports regarding the Warriors' contract offer
quotes.excerpt: There was never an offer from the Warriors for five years, 150 million.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: There's all these reports that he's turned down nine-figure deals. What's the truth about all those reports?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: There was never an offer from the Warriors for five years, 150 million. That never came on the table. In fact, to take it a step further, the Warriors never made an offer on an extension. Now, could Jonathan Kuminga have maybe taken some real discounted value? Possibly, but we never even got to really get there. The Warriors, if you look at what they're doing and you understand this business, they want clean books after this year. Now maybe if Stephen Curry extends or something happens from there, they'll decide that, but they wanted flexibility. They wanted the ability to possibly trade Jonathan Kuminga. They wanted to see what would happen. So there was no world anywhere that they were giving him five years, 150 million.

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The unusual nature of the Warriors' contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: Hall of Fame coach says you don't fit, front office owner say well let's give you money.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: What was the truth about the offers and why he chose this two-year, 13 million dollar deal?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: It set the table for the weirdness of probably the weirdest negotiation of all time, where a Hall of Fame coach comes out and says, 'This guy Jonathan Kuminga, he's a really good talented player, but he doesn't fit the roster with Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler.' And then on the flip side of that, you have the front office and owner offer him money in the 20s. Hall of Fame coach says you don't fit, front office owner say well let's give you money in the 20s. That doesn't happen. So we took a shorter deal because we knew that would be more tradeable, which kind of was what was going to happen.

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating the free agency market for Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: Bryson Graham was a big part of why he went to Atlanta.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: What was the truth about the deals in the Lakers, the Warriors, I heard Portland, Chicago?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: Chicago came in. Bryson Graham was a big part of why he went to Atlanta. He went from Atlanta to Chicago. And Bryson has a strong belief in Jonathan Kuminga, so Chicago became a real contender in this, but they're also in a different timeline obviously than Minnesota is right now. Portland also came in. They offered a pretty good deal. They got up with some player option and even was higher than Minnesota. And then there were the Lakers who were offering their concept. And what it all came down to at the end was, Jonathan Kuminga, where do you feel comfortable that you can play and enjoy basketball?

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.excerpt: Tim Connelly didn't want to let him go, but he knew it was not a great spot.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Is there anything else you can share about the process?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: Last year I had Josh Minott on Minnesota, who's a good player and flourished in Brooklyn, went from Boston to Brooklyn, but Tim Connelly didn't want to let him go, but he knew it was not a great spot here if he needs to play and he needs a platform to play. And he let him go. And that stuff was over the years for me let me know, okay, Tim, I know what you stand for and I know what you're saying to Jonathan Kuminga and it makes sense.

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.summary_phrase: The importance of organizational alignment for Jonathan Kuminga
quotes.excerpt: Here you have owner, GM, head coach, star player, all in complete alignment.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: What was the most important factor in this decision?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: Where's the cleanest basketball with the best organizational alignment? Because that's been part of the problem. You have different, and this happens in different organizations, but this has been the most played out one for as long as I've seen. Owner, GM, coach, here you have owner, GM, head coach, star player, all in complete alignment that this is the guy they want.

quotes.speaker: Aaron Turner
quotes.excerpt: Part of the problem with a sign-and-trade, which is tricky, the first three years cannot have optionability.

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: What about the Lakers? How close was he to becoming a Laker?

text_blocks.speaker: Aaron Turner
text_blocks.text: Part of the problem with a sign-and-trade, which is tricky, the first three years cannot have optionability. So I'm sure Rob Pelinka would have said, 'Hey, you guys can do a two-plus-one,' or I would think, we never really got there because it's not allowed. So because of that, it limited kind of the optionability the Lakers can offer because the deal had to be three years. So if you're going to tie somebody up three years going into their prime as a starting wing, locking in at 12 million dollars in this NBA is pretty decently below the mid-level.
